"你看到过我吗？我是住在你家院子里、石头下或花盆底下的“鼠妇”。我不是老鼠，也不是昆虫，更不是蜘蛛，我是虾的亲戚。“鼠妇”这个名字听起来很奇怪，不过，却是有原因的，那是因为……

























































































































[P4] 让人想不透的名字
—鼠妇
我会被叫作“鼠妇”，是因为
很久很久以前，我的祖先和老鼠同
住在洞穴中。有一天，我的祖先攀
爬在老鼠身上，跟着老鼠跑出洞
去，被人们看到了，他们就叫我
“鼠负”。后来，传来传去，“鼠负”
就变成了“鼠妇”。

“鼠妇”的名字是怎么来的？
1. 很久很久以前，鼠妇和老鼠一起住
在阴暗的洞穴中。
2. 有一天，当鼠妇趴在老鼠身上睡
觉时，老鼠却突然往洞外跑去。
3. 老鼠跑进厨房，厨房里煮饭的大
娘吓得大叫！
4. 后来，人们开始讨论，厨房的大娘
到底看到了什么。大家传来传去
就成了老鼠背着老婆跑进厨房！

啊，有老鼠！
鼠背上还背
着虫子！

▲ 鼠妇是群居动物，会一大群一起生
活。它们很怕光，所以喜欢住在阴暗
的地方。

[P5] 我不是“土鳖”或“木虱”
有些人叫我“土鳖”或“木虱”，因为我的居住地和它们很像。其实，我不是鳖，也不是虱，但我确实生活在土壤中，也经常出现在落叶、枯枝下，因为这些都是我最重要的食物，我离不开它们。
木虱属于昆虫，有三对脚，与鼠妇的身体一样有纹路。它们的体长只有0.6厘米，全身褐色，住在木头里。
你是谁？
我是木虱！

[P6] 鼠妇喜欢吃干枯的落叶、死掉的小虫，或是土壤里腐烂的有机物质，所以它们经常出现在花盆或落叶底下。
土鳖也是昆虫，分为头、胸、腹三节，身体有分节，脚上有细毛，体长约3厘米，全身黑褐色，生活在土壤中。
数日后
你又是谁？
我是土鳖！

[P7] 我也叫“潮虫”，因为我很需要水
除了生活在泥土里或落叶下，我住的地方也需要有水，最好是地面湿湿的那种地方，就像我的亲戚虾一样，我们都很需要水。我和虾都会通过蜕皮来长大，每一次蜕皮都会让我们身体的颜色变得不一样。
湿湿的，
真舒服。
好热哦！我要渴死了。
鼠妇蜕皮后长大
鼠妇会先脱掉后半段硬硬的外壳，露出新长出来的软壳。
我扭我扭。
几天后，再脱掉前半段的外壳。
哈，我长大了！
鼠妇幼虫会经过数次蜕皮，变成成虫，身体的颜色也会渐渐变黑。
原来，你蜕皮的方式跟我的一样啊！

[P8] 我蜷起来时就变成“丸子虫”“团子虫”或“豆虫”
啊，敌人出现了！
我有一个绝招，遇到危险的时候，为了保护自己，会把自己蜷起来，变成一颗小圆球。这时候，我看起来就像是一颗丸子、团子或豆子，所以，人们也叫我“丸子虫”“团子虫”或“豆虫”。
嘻嘻，别想吃我！
啊，别跑！
①遇到敌人或危险。
它在做什么呀？
②身体开始蜷曲。
③把所有的脚与触角都收进身体里。
④变成一颗小球，用硬硬的外壳来保护软软的肚子。
快跑！
8/12

[P9] 鼠妇的身体有很多节，可以很灵活地蜷成球状。它们体形扁平，有许多只脚，所以能轻易地爬上爬下，或钻入土壤的缝隙中。硬硬的外壳不仅能保护身体，也能防止体内的水分散失。

我也叫“西瓜虫”或“皮球虫”

也有人叫我“西瓜虫”或“皮球虫”，这是因为我的身体是一节一节的，蜷缩成圆球后，看起来就像是西瓜或小皮球的纹路。

触角

脚

鼠妇有7对脚，共14只，还有1对触角。9/12

[P10] 人们称我为“清道夫”
不管大家叫我什么名字，我都是身体
小小的，喜欢住在阴暗的、潮湿的地方，
身体能蜷成球形的小动物。
我喜欢吃落叶、枯枝和动物的死尸。
对了，人们还称呼我为“清道夫”。因为我
能处理部分垃圾，让地球保持干净。
鼠妇、白蚁、千足虫与
蚯蚓等小虫，都会吃掉
落叶或土壤里的有机
质，所以，它们都是地
球上的“分解者”。
鼠妇
白蚁
千足虫
蚯蚓

[P1] The Name of the Woodlouse
Written by Sun Wanling  Illustrated by Zhu Jiayu
Zhejiang Publishing United Group

[P2] The Name of the Woodlouse
Written by / Sun Wanling  Illustrated by / Zhu Jiayu
Zhejiang Publishing United Group
Zhejiang Children's Publishing House
2/12

[P4] A Name That's Hard to Figure Out
—Woodlouse
I am called 'woodlouse' because
long, long ago, my ancestors lived
in caves with mice. One day, my ancestors
climbed onto a mouse and followed it out
of the cave. When people saw this, they
called me 'mouse-carrier'. Later, as it spread,
'mouse-carrier' became 'woodlouse'.

How did the name 'woodlouse' come about?
1. Long, long ago, woodlice and mice lived
together in dark caves.
2. One day, when a woodlouse was sleeping
on a mouse, the mouse suddenly ran out of the cave.
3. The mouse ran into the kitchen, and the
woman cooking there screamed in fright!
4. Later, people began to discuss what
the woman in the kitchen had seen.
As the story spread, it became
'a mouse carrying its wife into the kitchen'!

Ah, there's a mouse!
It's carrying bugs on its back!

▲ Woodlice are social animals that live in large groups.
They are afraid of light, so they like to live in dark places.

[P5] I am not 'dirt crab' or 'wood louse'
Some people call me 'dirt crab' or 'wood louse' because my habitat is similar to theirs. In fact, I am not a crab, nor a louse, but I do live in soil and often appear under fallen leaves and dead branches, because these are my most important food sources, and I cannot live without them.
The wood louse is an insect with three pairs of legs, and its body has patterns similar to those of the pill bug. They are only 0.6 centimeters long, brown all over, and live inside wood.
Who are you?
I am the wood louse!

[P6] Woodlice like to eat dry fallen leaves, dead small insects, or decaying organic matter in the soil, so they often appear under flowerpots or fallen leaves.
Earth roaches are also insects, divided into head, thorax, and abdomen, with segmented bodies, fine hairs on their legs, about 3 cm long, dark brown all over, and live in the soil.
After several days
Who are you?
I am an earth roach!

[P7] I'm also called 'damp bug', because I need a lot of water.
Besides living in soil or under fallen leaves, the places I live in also need water, preferably damp ground. Just like my relative, the shrimp, we both need water. Both I and shrimp grow by molting. Each time we molt, our body color changes.
Damp, so comfortable.
It's so hot! I'm going to be thirsty to death.
After molting, the pill bug grows up
The pill bug will first shed the hard outer shell of its rear half, revealing the new soft shell.
I twist, I twist.
A few days later, shed the outer shell of the front half.
Ha, I've grown up!
The pill bug larvae will molt several times to become adults, and their body color will gradually turn black.
Originally, your molting method is the same as mine!

[P8] When I curl up, I become a 'meatball bug', 'dumpling bug', or 'bean bug'.
Ah, the enemy has appeared!
I have a special trick. When I encounter danger, to protect myself, I curl up into a small ball. At that moment, I look like a meatball, dumpling, or bean, so people also call me 'meatball bug', 'dumpling bug', or 'bean bug'.
Hehe, don't even think about eating me!
Ah, don't run!
① Encounter an enemy or danger.
What is it doing?
② The body begins to curl.
③ Tuck all legs and antennae inside the body.
④ Become a small ball, using a hard shell to protect the soft belly.
Run fast!
8/12

[P9] The body of a pill bug has many segments, allowing it to curl up into a ball very flexibly. They have a flat body shape and many legs, so they can easily climb up and down or burrow into soil cracks. Their hard outer shell not only protects their body but also prevents water loss.

I'm also called "Watermelon Bug" or "Rubber Ball Bug"

Some people call me "Watermelon Bug" or "Rubber Ball Bug" because my body is segmented, and when I curl into a ball, I look like the pattern of a watermelon or a small rubber ball.

Antennae

Legs

Pill bugs have 7 pairs of legs, totaling 14 legs, and 1 pair of antennae. 9/12

[P10] People call me the 'Sanitation Worker'
No matter what you call me, I am a small creature that likes to live in dark, damp places and can curl up into a ball.
I like to eat fallen leaves, twigs, and animal carcasses.
Yes, people also call me the 'Sanitation Worker' because I can process some waste and keep the Earth clean.
Isopods, termites, millipedes, and earthworms are all small insects that eat organic matter in fallen leaves or soil, so they are all 'decomposers' on Earth.
Isopod
Termite
Millipede
Earthworm
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《鼠妇的名字》的封面，展示了书名、作者和插画师信息，以及一只藏在树皮下的鼠妇的特写照片。
[P2] 本页为绘本《鼠妇的名字》的扉页，展示了书名、作者、插画师及出版社信息，并配有一张鼠妇蜷缩成球状的特写照片。
[P4] 本页解释了‘鼠妇’这个名字的由来，通过一个古代传说说明其祖先曾爬在老鼠背上被误认为是‘老鼠背着老婆’，并配图展示了鼠妇群居、怕光的生活习性。
[P5] 本页通过对话和文字说明，澄清鼠妇并非‘土鳖’或‘木虱’，并介绍了木虱的特征，同时展示了鼠妇与木虱在外观和习性上的区别。
[P6] 本页介绍了鼠妇的食性和栖息地，并通过文字和对话解释了土鳖的特征，同时配图展示了落叶腐烂的过程和两种生物在土壤中的互动。
[P7] 本页介绍了鼠妇（潮虫）需要潮湿环境的生活习性，并通过对话和插图展示了其蜕皮成长的过程，以及与虾类相似的蜕皮方式。
[P8] 本页通过对话和分步图解，介绍了鼠妇在遇到危险时会蜷缩成球的防御行为，并解释了其因此被称为“丸子虫”“团子虫”或“豆虫”的由来。
[P9] 本页通过文字和图片介绍了鼠妇的身体结构，包括其分节的身体、14只脚和1对触角，并解释了其被称为“西瓜虫”或“皮球虫”的原因，同时说明了其硬壳能保护身体并防止水分流失的特性。
[P10] 本页以第一人称介绍鼠妇被称为‘清道夫’的原因，因其以落叶、枯枝和动物尸体为食，帮助分解有机物、清理环境，并配图展示了鼠妇、白蚁、千足虫和蚯蚓等分解者在森林地表的活动场景。
[P11] 本页展示了一只鼠妇攀爬在蘑菇茎上的自然场景，背景为森林地面的落叶和泥土，画面聚焦于鼠妇与蘑菇的互动，体现其在潮湿环境中的栖息状态。
